result: Rail underside finish and inaccessible supports require revision

observations.rails: The rectangular rail supports are removable once a screwdriver reaches them at the appropriate angle. The first model course above them is stringy and loose; subsequent courses show local narrowing and glossy/color variation.
observations.prv_vent: A tall tree reaches the flat mouth lip; a self-supporting chamfer is requested.
observations.pisco_and_asse_receivers: Full-size enclosure walls block screwdriver access to the tiny supports. These interiors must print without supports.
observations.rear_bulkhead_bores: Color plates cover the wall bores, allowing teardrop roofs instead of supported circular crowns.
observations.valve_post_sockets: Small valve holes should print without supports.

user_words: I can't reach in that far to remove those tiny little supports.
The bulkhead holes on the back, why aren't those teardrop shaped?
I did get those normal supports out.
the first layer on top of the supports is stringy and loose and basically falling off

rail_cooling_review.inference: The photographs and reported texture motivate checking cooling and deposition on the newly bridged foundation; gloss alone does not measure temperature.
